i01.summary: Base size of ₹150 crore plus an equal green shoe, rated CRISIL A+/Stable, with effective yields from 8.64% to 10.00%. The window runs to October 5.
i01.title: Edelweiss opens a ₹300 crore NCD issue

i02.summary: Up to ₹700 crore including the green shoe. BSE listing is due within three working days of closing; watch the first trades for where the market prices it.
i02.title: Muthoot Fincorp Tranche V closes

i03.summary: The April issue carried an Acuite BBB-/Stable rating after the company moved agencies. A change of agency is worth checking for rating shopping.
i03.title: ICL Fincorp changes rating agency for its ninth issue

i04.summary: The consultation would bar terms like 'high yield' and 'high returns', celebrity endorsements and artificial urgency in bond ads. Comments closed September 11.
i04.title: SEBI proposes curbs on bond advertising

i05.summary: Platforms may now list IFSCA-regulated products, labelled as international and subject to FEMA/LRS, plus 54EC bonds with prescribed disclosures.
i05.title: SEBI widens what online bond platforms can offer

i06.summary: Co-investment is now limited to accredited investors, AIF overseas VC investment is capped at $1.5 billion industry-wide, and onboarding is stricter.
i06.title: New AIF master circular tightens co-investment and overseas limits

i07.summary: Managers must do due diligence so AIFs are not used to get around RBI stressed-asset norms or FEMA land-border rules. Relevant wherever private credit AIFs buy NBFC or real estate NCDs.
i07.title: AIF managers must guard against evergreening

i08.summary: A mid-June update to the AIF master circular covers retention of proceeds on winding up and introduces an inoperative-fund status.
i08.title: Winding-up rules and 'inoperative fund' status added

i09.summary: A comprehensive annual activity report replaces most quarterly reporting; the first revised quarterly report covers the June 2026 quarter.
i09.title: AIF reporting moves to annual plus limited quarterly

i10.summary: FPI limits stay at 6% (G-Secs), 2% (state securities) and 15% (corporate bonds). VRR now counts under general-route limits. The total debt limit rises from ₹15,51,646 crore (Apr-Sep 2026) to ₹16,32,640 crore (Oct 2026-Mar 2027).
i10.title: FPI debt limits held; VRR folded into general route

i11.summary: The rate ceiling on fresh 3-5 year FCNR(B) deposits was lifted, with a subsidised swap and CRR/SLR exemption. Banks paid up to 7.10%, drawing NRI dollars into bank liquidity.
i11.title: RBI opens an FCNR(B) swap window

i12.caution: Unverified: confirm against RBI's own notifications before acting.
i12.summary: RBI's June directions set September 30 as the end date. A recent report says the window shut on August 31 and deposit rates have since dropped.
i12.title: Conflicting reports on when the FCNR window ended

i13.summary: After the 2026 cuts, one market guide puts BBB NBFC issuers at roughly 400-600 bps over the G-Sec and AAA at 50-100 bps. Other sources put the 10-year near 6.9%, so set the benchmark to your own desk's number.
i13.title: Repo at 5.25%, 10-year G-Sec around 6.5-6.8%

i14.summary: The Supreme Court's 2018 Bar Council v A.K. Balaji ruling is cited as permitting non-lawyer funders; FEMA applies to foreign funders. Watch court and NCLT filings naming issuers or promoters as a credit signal.
i14.title: Litigation funding: allowed, but no central law

i15.summary: Sneaker and other fractional platforms have no dedicated regulator, and commentators argue they may be treated as collective investment schemes under the SEBI Act. A SEBI move here would signal wider retail-product scrutiny.
i15.title: Fractional collectibles face collective-scheme risk
